entries.note: The universal claim attributes a hidden industry intention to every discussion of these terms.

entries.test: Q1 2026 revenue disclosures, customer spending records and pricing changes would establish the revenue totals, their sources and whether customers subsequently reduced spending.
entries.note: The causal explanation and universal pullback claim require evidence beyond the revenue totals.

entries.test: OpenAI's published mathematical results and their assumptions would establish whether hallucination is unavoidable even with external harnesses and scripts.
entries.note: The hallucination assertion is testable; 'thoughts' and 'knowledge' lack comparably settled definitions. He adopts the OpenAI-attributed conclusion in his own voice.

entries.test: Industry revenue estimates, both labs' compute expenditures and financial statements, and hyperscaler spending records would establish the claimed share and funding flows.
entries.note: 'I estimate' qualifies a numerical estimate rather than stating a probability.
The sweeping historical comparison uses 'hysteria,' 'monocultural force' and 'grift' as polemical characterizations.
Capex plans and revenue disclosures are checkable components. They cannot settle the asserted exclusive motive that these companies have no other growth ideas.
Whether capabilities justify their cost is a judgment of worth without a specified return criterion.

entries.test: NVIDIA's capacity-backstop agreements and cloud providers' independently funded bookings, utilization and customer revenues would establish the backstops and the scale of underlying demand.
entries.note: The existence of a backstop alone does not establish the absence of demand.

entries.test: Comparable GPU operating costs and compute-service prices before and after an AI investment collapse would establish whether the collapse makes compute cheaper.
entries.note: In context, 'magically' emphasizes a substantive prediction about costs after a collapse.

entries.test: Public investment incentives, AI promotion and default product integrations, together with adoption data, would show whether promotion and forced integration cease when investor incentives disappear.
entries.note: 'Something that will ... end' most naturally refers to manufacturing consent and forced integration, not necessarily all AI demand.
The compute-to-price ratio is independently testable. It cannot establish the asserted private motivation of all subscribers.

entries.test: Compute usage by service tier, unsubsidized token costs and subscriber affordability data would establish whether overwhelmingly subsidized demand and the universal affordability assertion hold.
entries.note: The claim about 'anyone' is stronger than saying typical subscribers could not afford equivalent usage.

entries.test: Public comparisons of costs for equivalent AI workloads across capacity expansions and GPU generations would establish whether either has reduced costs.
entries.note: This denies a causal effect of additional compute and newer hardware.

entries.test: Following a $42 billion government investment for 5% of OpenAI, its financial disclosures and eventual survival or failure would test whether the funding merely delayed collapse.
entries.note: The proposition reverses the transaction: the government would receive the equity stake, while OpenAI would receive funding.

entries.test: Public capacity plans, projected utilization and rental rates, and customer spending excluding OpenAI and Anthropic would establish the implied annual revenue and remaining demand.
entries.note: 'I believe' introduces an asserted estimate, not an explicit chance or possibility.
Neither 'over-valued' nor 'no foreseeable path' supplies a shared valuation standard or assessment horizon.
The combined revenue forecast explicitly says 'likely.' The compute-spend estimate is a separately testable component.
'For all eternity' and 'so, forever' are sarcastic exaggerations about business viability.

entries.test: AI compute demand and annual spending through 2030, compared with July 2026 levels, together with industry failures and investment losses would test the asserted necessary condition for avoiding a collapse.
entries.note: The demand threshold has a 2030 horizon; 'carnage' plainly refers here to a severe industry financial collapse.

entries.test: After hyperscaler capex and NVIDIA GPU demand decline, public ODM, memory and storage revenues and semiconductor-sector results would show whether the predicted prolonged downturn occurs and whether any bailout reverses it.
entries.note: 'Kill the revenues' has a plain contextual reading of severe revenue declines.

entries.test: Applicable spending law, congressional proceedings and public polling on a proposed $50 billion or $100 billion AI bailout would establish the approval requirement and predicted bipartisan opposition.
entries.note: The normalization broadens 'those on the left who've grown tired of Big Tech' to 'the left.' The legal component can already be assessed.

entries.test: Major technology companies' solvency, liquidity and continuing operations immediately after an AI bubble collapse would establish whether the vast majority remain financially viable.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives 'fine' a financial-survival meaning despite market losses and impairments.
NVIDIA's ranking prediction explicitly says 'likely,' and the proposed worst outcomes are framed as what he 'could see.'
The exclusive causal explanation rests on a collective hidden motive to conceal a lack of ideas. The investment justification is also a value judgment.

entries.test: Technology-sector valuations following an AI bubble collapse would show whether a broader downward revaluation extends beyond AI companies.
entries.note: The outcome depends on the AI bubble ending. 'I think ... will' states an expectation; the drafter's 'likely' modality is not his wording.
This advocates ending the era and allowing unsuccessful businesses to fail.
